services.name: Player_ResolveTerrainContact
services.behavior: When TERRAIN_STATE is set and PLAYER_VY is nonnegative, handles inactive terrain response by stopping vertical motion, applying directional push facing/animation, aligning the player grid, selecting camera thresholds, and setting PLAYER_INTERACTION_TRANSITION_LOCK. If a vertical stop is active, it clears the response state and performs the same alignment.

services.name: Player_AlignYToCameraGrid
services.behavior: Writes PLAYER_Y = ((PLAYER_WORLD_Y & 0xFFF0) | 4) - WORLD_CAMERA_Y and restores CAMERA_HORIZONTAL_THRESHOLD to 0xB0.

evidence.frame_path: Game_FrameUpdateLoop calls the terrain response/motion region before MovementVM and actor collision; Player_ResolveTerrainContact calls Player_SelectInteractionAnimation and Player_AlignYToCameraGrid on contact and response-stop branches.
evidence.directional_contact: The contact routine sets PLAYER_FACING_X_FLIP to 0 or 0xFF for right/left push flags, advances the 0x00FFF16A interaction animation index modulo 0x28, and refreshes the interaction animation when the gate permits.
evidence.camera_contract: Terrain push-down and push-up states select camera vertical thresholds 0x130 and 0x1B0 with a seven-frame camera update delay; the neutral contact path restores thresholds 0xB0/0x150 and clears the delay.

limitations: The exact semantic label for the 0x00FFF16A animation index remains an implementation detail of the interaction-animation selector.
This finding records the static contact contract and does not add a new runtime trace.
conclusion: The player terrain path now distinguishes vertical-response correction from terrain contact resolution: Player_ApplyTerrainResponse handles the query/stop response, Player_ResolveTerrainContact handles non-rising contact and directional push state, and Player_AlignYToCameraGrid owns the local-Y/camera alignment formula.
